title: Mars regolith roads, traffic loads and road-versus-rail trade-off audit for OTA-TEC-0090
question: Source-grounded audit of the exact OTA-TEC-0090 Mars route-corridor dossier. Assess: (1) what Mars regolith/simulant geotechnical evidence supports about bearing, shear, compaction, traction and prepared surfaces while keeping site-specific design values open; (2) realistic construction and maintenance options for graded/compacted regolith tracks and locally stabilized or sintered surfaces; (3) dust, thermal cycling, settlement and repeated wheel-load effects; (4) rolling-resistance and vehicle-energy implications of prepared versus unprepared routes; (5) what evidence exists for rail or guided transport concepts on Mars/Moon and under which high-throughput, repetitive freight conditions they might outperform road vehicles; (6) why no universal road-to-rail crossover point can be claimed without load, distance, construction energy and maintenance assumptions; and (7) wording requiring narrowing or [H]/[OFFEN] status. Do NOT set road widths, axle loads, network geometry, build costs, travel-time bonuses, rail unlocks or other NOXIA balancing values.
why_now: OTA-TEC-0090 is an uncovered mapped infrastructure object and explicitly remains ENTWURF pending geotechnical load limits and a source-grounded road-versus-rail trade-off.
real_world_anchor: Mars/lunar regolith geotechnics and simulant testing; planetary rover terramechanics; prepared-surface construction concepts; space-settlement freight road/rail/guided-transport studies.
novelty_reason: Extends rover-level mobility evidence into linear infrastructure and throughput-dependent road/rail system design without re-auditing the rover itself.
